title: Uppercase alphabet sampler in cross-stitch
subtitle: All 26 letters plus numerals 0 to 9 on 14-count Aida
excerpt: An uppercase alphabet sampler stitches all 26 letters and the ten digits in a clean 7-stitch-tall block font. The piece is 130-by-90 stitches on 14-count Aida and uses a single floss colour. Finished size is about 23 x 16 cm. The chart doubles as a reference sheet for designing custom word pieces.
sourceNotes: Block alphabet for cross-stitch. Uppercase alphabets for needlework appear throughout the sampler tradition, including examples in Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776.

content.text: An uppercase alphabet sampler lays all 26 letters and the ten digits across a 130-by-90 stitch piece on 14-count
. The block font is 7 stitches tall with a 1-stitch gap between letters and a 2-stitch gap between rows. One
colour covers the whole piece. The finished size is about 23 x 16 cm and it is as much a working chart as a display piece, once framed, you can read off letter shapes for any custom text project.

items.name: 14-count Aida, white or cream
items.substitutions: Any colour Aida; choose a floss colour with good contrast against it

items.name: DMC floss
items.qty: 3 skeins of your chosen colour (a single navy blue like 823 or deep green like 500 reads clearly)

content.text: Find the centre of the fabric. The chart centre falls roughly in the M-N area of the first row. Mark the fabric centre and identify the corresponding chart position before threading the needle.

Work the first row (A to M) from the centre outward, then complete the second row (N to Z), and the numeral row last. Working each row left-to-right after placing the first letter is easier than jumping between rows.

Check the row alignment after each complete letter: the base of each letter should sit on the same counted row as all other letters in that row. A one-row slip in a letter is easy to miss within a letter but obvious when you step back.

items.symptom: One letter is one row higher or lower than its neighbours
items.cause: The letter was started from the wrong counted row rather than from the consistent baseline.
items.fix: Always count from the fabric centre or a nearby basted grid line to confirm the baseline of each letter before stitching the first cross.

content.text: Once the full alphabet feels easy, try the family name banner or house name sampler. Both use these letter shapes in personalised pieces with decorative borders.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. The default for beginners. Counted in squares per inch: 11ct, 14ct, 16ct, and 18ct are the common counts.

The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch. Each skein is made of six strands twisted together loosely; the stitcher strips out the number of strands needed for the fabric count (two strands for 14-count Aida) and threads them together.
